The issue is clear. In `fu.py` line 504, `rv.exp < 0` is called on a complex exponent. The fix is to check if the exponent is comparable (real) before doing the comparison.

The fix: add a check for `rv.exp.is_integer` early on (or check `rv.exp.is_real`). Looking at the logic, the function deals with integer exponents (it checks `rv.exp == 2`, `rv.exp == 4`, `rv.exp % 2`), so we should return early if the exponent is not an integer.

arguments.command: cd /testbed && sed -i 's/        if (rv.exp < 0) == True:/        if not rv.exp.is_real:\n            return rv\n        if (rv.exp < 0) == True:/' sympy/simplify/fu.py
